label: a6-130-ex-neighbourhood-indexed-net-converging-to-a-closure-point
tail:
No fatal defects found.

The proof steps are valid: the index set is a directed preorder, the net lies in \(A\), and it converges to \(p\) by the definition of net convergence. The cited dependencies provide the necessary facts—neighbourhood intersections are neighbourhoods ([L2] from `def-neighbourhood-top`), convergence means eventual membership in every neighbourhood ([L3] from `def-net-convergence-and-cluster-point`), and the existence of a net from `thm-closure-characterised-by-nets` together with [L3] yields that every neighbourhood of \(p\) meets \(A\) ([L1]). That last step is a trivial inference for a competent reader. No choice principle is used beyond what the library already assumes. The title matches the content.

N fatal, 0 nonfatal
